architecture.mechanism: Multi-bearing, multi-objective collaborative optimization of the lubrication system that reduces circulating flow rate and oil consumption by jointly targeting minimum oil film thickness across multiple operating conditions.
architecture.intervention: Redesign the engine lubrication circuit to use a multi-bearing feed layout with calibrated oil-jet sizing, then run a multi-objective optimization (e.g., AMESim + HEEDS) that simultaneously maximizes bearing oil-film thickness and minimizes total circulated oil flow at idle, mid, and rated rpm; re-specify the oil pump capacity and restrictors to the optimized flow, and switch the oil specification to a manufacturer-approved viscosity grade that sustains the optimized film thickness (avoiding the conventional 5W-30 that was reported).
architecture.expected_effect: Eliminates the low-oil warning and eliminates top-up needs between factory oil-change intervals by reducing oil consumption through lowered circulating flow rate (paper shows 6% reduction) and eliminating over-lubrication, while preserving bearing protection under all operating speeds.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument the vehicle to record oil mass at each oil change and at every 1,000 miles over two consecutive factory-recommended oil-change intervals; also measure main-bearing oil-film thickness (or proxy via oil pressure/temperature at bearings) at 800, 1800, and 2800 rpm on a dynamometer. The intervention is falsified if (a) any low-oil warning occurs within the interval, (b) more than 0.25 L of make-up oil is required per 1,000 miles, or (c) minimum oil-film thickness falls below the manufacturer's spec at any of the three test speeds.
